reviewer: Codex runtime_recovery independent AI language reviewer; not a human or subject-matter reviewer
scope: Independent selected-sense, definition, example and editorial placement review for three narrow proposals. No source, media, morphology, domain, expression or whole-entry acceptance is granted.

fresh_evidence.rendered_web_consultation: The reviewer independently opened and inspected the selected Oxford and Collins sections for all three terms, the CEFR-J profile and attribution/methodology pages, and the British Council lesson. These observations were made during this review, separately from the author's frozen captures.
fresh_evidence.body_retention: Complete remote response bodies were transient and were not retained. The direct receipt records response hashes, sizes, selected attributes and profile rows; these are observations, not a retained-body archive. Rendered web observations have no locally retained body hash.
fresh_evidence.oxford_hash_difference: The fresh Oxford body hashes differ from the author's earlier hashes. Selected-sense metadata agrees; fresh observations are not represented as byte-identical copies of the author capture.

frozen_author_evidence.use: Frozen proposal, context, historic hold records and source ledger were read as author evidence. Rechecking hashes does not turn those captures into fresh independent source retrieval.

sources.selected_section: postpone_sng_1; moving a planned event or action to a later time
sources.observation: The selected meaning supports the planned-review example and the postpone something until a later time pattern. The C1 source placement is retained as contrary placement evidence.
excluded: general rescheduling to either an earlier or a later time

sources.selected_section: Planned-event sense in the learner entry
sources.observation: The selected event sense and postponing a planned activity agree with the draft. B1+ is recorded literally and is not converted to B2.

sources.selected_section: unsafe_sng_1, sense 1: dangerous place, thing or activity
sources.observation: The selected danger sense supports unsafe storage area. Personal vulnerability and the British legal-evidence/conviction sense are separate and excluded. A missing level supplies neither B1 nor B2 evidence.

sources.selected_section: Sense 1: dangerous buildings, machines, activities or areas
sources.observation: The dangerous-area sense agrees with the storage-area example. The selected section has no observed level. Personal danger and legal-evidence uses remain outside the decision.

sources.selected_section: hazard_sng_1, noun: possible danger, damage or cause of harm
sources.observation: The potential-cause noun supports the draft definition and loose-cable example. The C1 source placement remains visible as contrary placement evidence.

sources.selected_section: Count noun for a potential danger or risk
sources.observation: The noun agrees with potential harm. The verb senses involving guessing or risking, and golf or gambling uses, do not support this entry and are excluded.

sources.original_creator: Yukio Tono, Tono Laboratory, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies
sources.evidence_scope: Headword/POS recognition-vocabulary placement. Rows contain no selected-sense identifiers and do not certify productive mastery or this course's contexts.
sources.citation: Tono, Yukio / Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. CEFR-J Vocabulary Profile, version 1.5. Consulted through the Open Language Profiles hosting copy on 17 October 2026.

sources.observation: The README attributes the CEFR-J profile to Tono Laboratory/TUFS and requires proper attribution for research or commercial use. Its CC BY-SA 4.0 statement applies to the separate Octanove C1/C2 dataset; that label is not assigned here to the CEFR-J CSV.
sources.acquisition: Reference consultation only. No complete profile body or new game asset is packaged.

sources.publisher: CEFR-J / Tono Laboratory, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies
sources.observation: The methodology describes textbook-corpus vocabulary arranged by broadly CEFR-aligned materials and supplemented with English Vocabulary Profile evidence. Its scope is recognition vocabulary through B2. The official download page advertises version 1.6 dated 24 March 2020; the independently checked hosting file is version 1.5. No assumption is made that version 1.6 contains unchanged rows.
sources.retention: English reviewer paraphrase only; no full page text is copied.

sources.selected_section: Task 2B asks learners to infer highlighted vocabulary and explicitly includes hazard as a potential cause of accidents.
sources.evidence_scope: Lesson-level teaching evidence for the broad potential-cause noun; not an official per-word CEFR certificate and not support for every specialized hazard compound.
